yeah i would recommend this game to other players

Can't really recommend or not recommend it if you're really that interested in playing it. Get this on a sale. 

The main game/story is very good. A bit shorter than I expected, but once I found out there was bonus content with the coop, cosmetic unlocks, and perks, I initially felt like I would get my money's worth out of the game. I quickly got the hang of the mechanics in the main store as you circulate gun-melee-finisher gameplay. Now, I've played and beat games with parry/dodge mechanics before, including several souls titles such as Sekiro, so I know the meaning of "git gud" as much as anyone worth their salt. One I finished the story, I started looking into running the stratagem missions to earn points to unlock gear and perk points....and while some times these missions go smoothly, some of these missions are just impossible to say the least. I had a mission with modifiers that cut my melee and long range shot down by 70%. In a game that relies on needing to circulate your weapons in order to maximize DPS and survivability, this combo basically cripples your character. You might use the melta weapons or an auto rifle to get round this, but you'll burn through ammo extremely quick without viable melee or long range impact. This game relies on you being able to use ALL of your weapons in order to be effective, so having modifiers that nullify one or more of your kit (especially melee), effectively ruins the game on a cheap gimmick.

The game's bonus content and endgame replayability was something I looked forward to as a casual player, but I am beginning to realize this isn't really a casual game if you are seeking decent points for unlocks or perks. If it were simply a matter of getting better at the combat system, I'd not find much to complain about, but when the game basically stops you from using its mechanics through a modifier, I'm just not going to play.

The combat was amazing but the game overall got repetitive in longer sessions. Go to one area, kill (x) amount of enemies, have the occasional breakup with half-assed objectives, that sort of thing. Which sure, I wouldn't have an issue with if it wasn't the whole game. The real shining star is the multiplayer. PvP is buns, it's like Destiny 2's Crucible without rng guns, but the PvE is incredibly fun. Having a good combat system plus someone you can actually stand to listen to saved this. Also the Thunder Hammer rips.
